title: Case study
description: The canonical twelve-section case-study structure, with MISSING EVIDENCE as a first-class value. An unevidenced section is the string 'MISSING EVIDENCE' — never plausible prose, never a hedge. 'Early results were encouraging' is a fabrication wearing a hedge, and it is worse than the gap because a reader cannot spot it.

status.description: 'published' is set by a human publishing it, never by the agent.

publishable.description: The agent may only ever write false. There is no automated path from 'the fields are filled in' to 'this is on the website making claims about a real client'. A human publishing it is what changes this, by hand, outside the agent.

descriptor.description: The anonymous form, e.g. 'a Series A medical-device company'. Always present, because anonymised-but-true beats named-but-embellished and is available without waiting for a permission conversation.

granted_by.description: Who granted it. Silence, an old email, and 'they would probably be fine with it' are not permission.

record.description: Where the permission is recorded, so it can be produced if questioned.

constraints.description: May legitimately be empty — sometimes there were none worth naming.

related_capabilities.description: Drawn from the site's own capability list. Not invented.

evidence_gaps.description: The deliverable when evidence is short: a precise list of what to ask for and who can supply it. 'We are missing the outcome' is not actionable; 'ask whether the launch metric can be quoted' is.

nothing_inferred.description: An explicit assertion that every value came from a named input. A run that cannot make this statement has failed.

not_responsible_for.description: Stated explicitly. An unbounded role reads as an inflated one.

alternative_rejected.description: THE REJECTED OPTION IS THE CREDIBILITY. A case study with no discarded alternative reads as a description of the only thing anyone could have done.

outcome.description: Something a third party could verify. Never inferred, never estimated, never softened into an adjective.

observable.description: 'The site launched on 3 March' is an outcome. 'Engagement improved' without a measurement is not.

verifiable_by.description: How a sceptic could check it.

value.description: Verbatim as supplied. Never rounded up, never reframed as a multiple.

permitted.description: A metric may only appear if permission.metrics_permitted is true.
